title: Twelve Sections and One Blank Heading
subtitle: 划分与部门 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 划分与部门（科学与技术·分类与划分）
meta: 主题语境：划分与部门（科学与技术·分类与划分）　|　核心词汇：division　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 division 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the editor ① made a division that no reader in the town would have noticed, and he said the making was the whole of the chapter. The ② division, meaning the splitting and not the section, ran twelve parts and stayed unnumbered in the text; a division, he said, is the only thing in a chapter that is judged by how long it is left unheaded.

Every ③ division in that text had the same blank heading above it, and the ④ division at the end, meaning the one they kept for the appendix and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever queried twice. A division, his assistant said, is nine parts order and one part somebody willing to make; the editor said the order is the part that fills twelve parts.

The registrar meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the division was the whole of the office, meaning the section and not the splitting. The ⑥ division, meaning the section and not any of that, is the only thing in an office that everybody names and nobody visits; division, she said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a splitting and a section. She said the section is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ division had become a line in a table of contents, and the table had become an argument about the blank heading. The ⑧ division of the whole thing, the editor wrote in April, was one text and twelve parts of ordering; division, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to number. She said the numbering was never mentioned.

The ⑨ division I remember is the one at the end, which was numbered in 1971 and is still described as the strangest in the text. A ⑩ division, the assistant said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being numbered; every division, she said, is a section that has agreed to look like a splitting. She said the section was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 划分；分割（指正文里作出的那一次）
B. n. 划分（指那个分开行为本身，与那个部门相对）
C. 固定搭配：make a division 作出一次划分
D. n. 划分（指留给附录用的那一次）
E. n. 划分；分界（抽象总称，指一整篇正文的划分之法）
F. n. 部分；章节（指目录上写到、被排定的那一块）
G. n. 部门；处（指机关里被称呼的那个单位）
H. n. 部门（抽象总称，指人人叫得出名却无人到访的那个）

items.q: made a division that no reader in the town would have noticed
The division, meaning the splitting and not the section
the division was the whole of the office
the division had become a line in a table of contents
The division of the whole thing
A division, the assistant said in 1973

answers.why: make a division 意为“作出一次划分”，1950 年编者作出了一次全镇没有一位读者会注意到的划分。
division 意为“划分”，指那个分开行为本身而不是那个部门，它分为十二个部分而在正文里没有编号。
division 意为“划分、分割”，指那篇正文里每一次划分，每一次上方都是同一个空白的标题。
division 意为“划分”，指留给附录用的那一次，是唯一有人质疑过两次的。
division 意为“部门、处”，指机关里被称呼的那个单位，注册主任说这个单位就是那间机关的全部。
division 意为“部门”，指人人叫得出名却无人到访的那个而不是那个分开行为，是机关里人人都叫得出名、却无人到访的东西。
division 意为“部分、章节”，指目录上写到、被排定的那一块，到 1958 年这一划分成了目录里的一行。
division 意为“划分、分界”，编者四月写道，整件事的划分之法是一篇正文和十二个部分的排序。
division 意为“划分”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1971 年编上号，至今仍被说成正文里最奇的一次。
division 为抽象总称，助手 1973 年说，一次划分是唯一会因为被编号而变得更好的东西。
